verifications.note: Fixed on this candidate. docs/architecture/erd.md (lines 197-200) lists the three views as read models with their source migration, and docs/architecture/data-dictionary.md has a new 'Views (read models)' section with one subsection per view: actor_display (0001), business_unit_closure (0001) and scope_node (0002). Each gives its columns, types, purpose and source query. I migrated a fresh PostgreSQL 16 database with the candidate and compared it with the docs. information_schema.views returns exactly actor_display, business_unit_closure and scope_node. Their columns and types (actor_display user_id uuid and display_name text; business_unit_closure ancestor_id, descendant_id and organization_id uuid, depth integer; scope_node scope_type text, scope_id, organization_id, business_unit_id and transformation_id uuid) match the dictionary tables exactly. mth_app has SELECT only on all three, as documented. The documented definitions match the SQL in 0001_identity_access.sql:62 and :93 (recursion capped at depth < 10) and 0002_transformation.sql:48 (UNION ALL of organization, business_unit and transformation). The claim that the views are pinned also holds: packages/db/src/schema.ts:282 VIEW_NAMES, and catalogue.test.ts asserts it ('marks exactly the views as views', which passed in the integration run). The ERD also documents the new 0009 trigger business_unit_hierarchy_guard (erd.md:201), which I observed installed on business_unit.
